clinician.trajectory_summary: A 9-year-old girl with genetically confirmed Mowat-Wilson syndrome (ZEB2 p.Gln694Ter mutation) presented to the Children's Outpatient Ophthalmology Clinic with visual pathway conduction disorders, convergent strabismus, and astigmatism. Initial ophthalmologic examination revealed: convergent strabismus (alternating, 15-20° on Hirschberg test) with preserved visual function (object following bilaterally, normal pupillary responses, full extraocular motility); temporal optic nerve pallor with subtle inferior disc elevation in the right eye; minor posterior synechiae bilaterally; and significant bilateral astigmatism (RE: −0.5 Dsph −6.0 Dcyl ax 178°; LE: −1.0 Dsph −6.5 Dcyl ax 162°). Ocular ultrasound demonstrated optic nerve drusen. Within less than a year, cataracts developed (total cortical in RE, partial cortical in LE), necessitating bilateral cataract surgery with foldable IOL implantation. Post-operative fundus examination confirmed optic nerve pallor with pigment regrouping in the right eye. At 3-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated visual recovery with restored object following and normal FVEP results. The case demonstrates the neuroophthalmologic manifestations of MWS, including optic nerve pallor, strabismus, refractive error, and cataract formation, consistent with the known genetic diagnosis and systemic features (psychomotor retardation, epileptic seizures, Hirschsprung's disease, patent ductus arteriosus, aortic valve stenosis, corpus callosum dysgenesis, and ventricular dilatation).
